entry.summary: AI Scientist Discovered Robust Quantum Control arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper introduces QORA, a multi-agent AI framework that combines theoretical reasoning with automated experimental calibration and control to discover quantum control sequences in a closed loop. Applied to a dense ensemble of spin-1 nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, it found AID-ROD sequences that nearly double the measured spin coherence time compared with the human-designed DROID-C3PO sequence. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report an AI framework discovering pulse sequences that nearly double spin coherence in spin-1 NV centers over DROID-C3PO, with a suppression hierarchy.

entry.title: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound for python's lunch decoding
entry.summary: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound on python's lunch decoding arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies the cost of decoding bulk information in holographic tensor networks, linked to the python's lunch conjecture about exponential post-selection costs. In a Haar random oracle model, the authors prove that recovering even one logical bit with constant average advantage requires Ω(2^{m/2}) queries. Combined with an amplitude amplification upper bound, the query complexity at constant decoding accuracy is Θ(2^{m/2}). The paper also comments on other admissible unitary ensembles. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a tight Ω(2^{m/2}) query lower bound for python's lunch decoding in a Haar random oracle model, matching an amplitude amplification upper bound.

entry.title: An axiomatic foundation for optimized certainty equivalents
entry.summary: An axiomatic foundation for optimized certainty equivalents arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper provides economic axioms that characterize Optimized Certainty Equivalents (OCEs), a major class of risk measures that includes Mean-Variance, Expected Shortfall, and the Entropic Risk Measure. It introduces the Fair-Coin Compensation axiom, which together with Strong Risk Aversion and Normalization characterizes OCEs, and it interprets this axiom through transfers that offset risk from a coin-toss assignment of two losses. Additional axioms such as Monotonicity, Positive Homogeneity with Prudence, and Fair-Coin Independence yield standard OCEs, Expected Shortfall, and the Entropic Risk Measure, respectively. The authors also axiomatize the Mean-Variance criterion using a new Equal-Mean Randomization axiom. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce Fair-Coin Compensation to axiomatically characterize OCEs and special cases including Expected Shortfall and the Entropic Risk Measure.

entry.title: HandRSI: A framework where AI repeatedly improves hand pose estimation from first-person video.
entry.summary: HandRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Hand Pose Estimation arXiv · Nov 17, 2026HandRSI is a framework that improves 3D hand pose estimation from egocentric video through repeated self-improvement. Coding agents refine the inference harness, and the video estimator is trained by selective distillation on frames with and without ground truth. The paper reports lower pose error and jitter on HOT3D and ARCTIC, and better results than nine re-run published methods on all ten metrics under a unified protocol. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose recursive coding-agent refinement of the inference harness alternating with estimator distillation; they report large MPJPE-p reductions on HOT3D and ARCTIC and gains over nine re-

entry.title: Long-context generation as a sampling problem at high temperature
entry.summary: Long-Context Generation Is a Sampling Problem (When You Turn Up the Heat) arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper tests 29 open-weight language models from 1B to 122B parameters on ten benchmarks and needle retrieval up to one million tokens. Samplers that keep their candidate-token pool small and stable as temperature rises, such as top-nsigma, keep their accuracy, while samplers that admit low-probability tokens, such as top-p and top-k, collapse. The authors explain this through candidate-pool size and release all code and data. ★★★★ Notable: The authors attribute long-generation degradation to sampler candidate-pool size and test 29 open models across ten benchmarks plus million-token needle retrieval, with impact on coding agents and lon

entry.title: When Lower Harm Misleads: Auditing Concept Corrections
entry.summary: When Lower Harm Misleads: Auditing Concept Corrections arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes a correction audit, a reproducible protocol that separates harm reduction from genuine improvement when experts correct concept predictions. Experiments on breast-ultrasound and CUB data show that objectives lowering harm can give up useful gain and raise negative log-likelihood. The authors conclude that lower harm indicates better corrections only when read together with useful gain, absolute risk and the starting prediction. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a correction audit separating harm from useful gain, showing lower harm can mislead, with reports across breast-ultrasound and CUB experiments.

entry.title: Thinking Longer Raises LLM Shopping Agents' Confidence, Not Their Accuracy
entry.summary: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper tests whether giving large language models more reasoning effort helps them choose better products when acting as autonomous shopping agents. The authors benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice tasks built from WebShop, Amazon SQID, and Wayfair WANDS. They find that more thinking effort does not meaningfully improve decision quality, but it significantly raises the models' stated confidence. Most models are poorly calibrated at every effort level, and errors are strongly correlated, with several models often picking the same wrong product. ★★★★ Notable: The authors benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks, finding reasoning effort raises confidence but not correctness, plus poor calibration and shared errors.

entry.title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: a near-optimal low-bit quantization format with a tiny decoder
entry.summary: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper proposes Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors that are written once and read many times. Its decoder multiplies a state by two coefficients and uses the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table, and one decoder covers bit widths from 1 to 6. In LLM weight quantization without fine-tuning on Llama 3.1 8B and 70B Instruct, CPTC has the lowest KL divergence to the unquantized model at every tested bit width compared with QTIP's codebooks, by up to 27%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a two-multiplication, 64-byte-table trellis decoder beating QTIP codebooks on KL divergence for Llama 3.1 8B and 70B, and hardware integration.

entry.title: Pathology Randomization for Zero-Shot Brain MRI Anomaly Detection
entry.summary: Pathology Randomization for Synthetic Priors and Zero-Shot Detection arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper presents PathoDraw, a generative model of brain MRI that includes pathology. It samples lesions on healthy anatomy to create label maps, renders them contrast-agnostically, and uses one network to estimate healthy anatomy and signed intensity deviation. Without training on real pathology, the single model performs zero-shot detection on public stroke, tumor, and white matter hyperintensity datasets and archived clinical scans, matching or exceeding contrast-specific detectors trained on real data. The same generator also trains networks for super-resolution and registration in the presence of pathology. ★★★★ Notable: The authors apply pathology randomization to synthetic priors, reporting zero-shot lesion detection across contrasts with one model, compared against contrast-specific detectors.

entry.title: Conserved verdicts and drifting commitments: how overthinking can harm reasoning models.
entry.summary: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking arXiv · Nov 17, 2026Reasoning models can lose a correct answer by continuing to think after reaching it. The paper argues that deciding whether to stop requires comparing the probability that the answer would be correct if stopped now (commitment) with the probability that the final answer is correct (verdict). On MATH-500, continuing at all 379 points where DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B held a correct answer lost 3.6 points on average (95% CI [2.2, 5.2]), with the loss concentrated in a few problems. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a commitment-verdict gap for stopping decisions and split accuracy curves into within-chain and running-set components, reporting measurements on MATH-500 and OlympiadBench.

entry.title: Certainty-equivalence control with near-logarithmic regret for degenerate LQR problems
entry.summary: Polylogarithmic Regret via Certainty Equivalence in Degenerate LQR arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies online linear quadratic control with singular input penalties. The authors prove that a certainty-equivalence algorithm with a short initial exploration phase achieves O(log²T) expected regret over T interactions when controller identifiability holds. They also give an Ω(√T) minimax lower bound for a family of systems that includes one where controller identifiability fails. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show singular input penalties relax identifiability, giving O(log^2 T) expected regret for certainty equivalence and an Ω(√T) minimax lower bound.

entry.title: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Rechecking Adversarial Face Privacy Methods
entry.summary: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Re-evaluating Adversarial Facial Privacy arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper argues that published face-privacy methods were tested by feeding whole photos or detector boxes to recognition models, while deployed systems first align and crop faces, which inflates reported protection. The authors re-score the same files through a realistic alignment step, show that a paired cosine shift measures the effect more reliably than success-rate differences, and find that optimising through a differentiable alignment operator recovers much of the lost performance. They also report that four thresholds inherited since 2021 produce higher false-accept rates on whole images than on aligned crops. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that evaluation input mismatch and a paired cosine shift metric were validated on three unseen recognizers and a commercial system, affecting face-privacy evaluation.

entry.title: Lost in a Few Heads: Fixing Block Selection Errors in Sparse Attention
entry.summary: Lost in a Few Heads: Diagnosing and Repairing Block Selection in Sparse Attention arXiv · Nov 17, 2026Sparse attention models read only a few key blocks per query, which can sharply reduce long-context retrieval accuracy. The paper shows the loss comes from the selector ranking the key information too low, not from running out of budget, and identifies a small set of attention heads responsible. Using full attention in those heads or a 4-bit scorer recovers most of the lost accuracy without any training. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use exact attention mass as an oracle to locate a few blind heads that miss the needle, and report multi-key retrieval rising from 54.1% to 97.5% on MiniCPM4.1-8B at 64K.

entry.title: Polynomial-time decoding of quadratic and generalized quadratic residue codes up to half the square-root bound
entry.summary: A polynomial-time decoding algorithm up to half the square-root bound for quadratic residue and generalized quadratic residue codes arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies binary quadratic residue (QR) codes and their generalization, generalized quadratic residue (GQR) codes, whose minimum distance satisfies the square-root bound. The authors give a deterministic algorithm that, for every odd prime power q congruent to ±1 mod 8, corrects every error pattern of weight at most ⌊(√q−1)/2⌋ in the binary GQR code of length q. The algorithm runs in O(q^{9/2}) operations in F_q. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first polynomial-time decoder for GQR codes, correcting up to half the square-root bound, adapting Kopparty's character-value recovery tools with O(q^{9/2}) operations.

entry.title: Maximizing entropy of cube projections
entry.summary: Entropy maximization for cube projections arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper proves that in every dimension n≥150, one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz for these dimensions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove that in dimensions n≥150 equal-magnitude directions maximize entropy of cube projections, resolving the Eskenazis–Nayar–Tkocz conjecture in those dimensions.

entry.title: Can Language Models Rewrite Their Own Weights? A study of self-editing parameters through reasoning, without training
entry.summary: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper asks whether a language model can improve itself by rewriting its own weights through its own reasoning, without gradients or training. A 27B model diagnoses its failures and edits the weights behind them, becoming 6.6 points more accurate on 490 unseen problems. The approach needs only an open model and a few hours on one GPU, and the model can also repair a damaged copy of itself. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a model rewriting its own weights via reasoning without gradients, validated on unseen math and six image benchmarks across a model family.

entry.title: Bajillion: a cryptographic clearing protocol for micropayments
entry.summary: Bajillion: Cryptographic Clearing for Micropayments arXiv · Nov 17, 2026As AI agents increasingly browse on behalf of people, the ad-funded web model may weaken, so paying per request becomes a possible replacement. This paper presents Bajillion, a clearing protocol for scalable micropayments in which an untrusted operator issues preconfirmations and periodically posts only net balances on chain. The authors state that a malicious operator can only omit payments, never overdraw senders or misdirect transfers. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a dispute-free clearing protocol for AI-agent micropayments, define an ideal functionality, and report a proof that it realizes it.

entry.title: Knowing Which, Not How Much: Language Models Rank Party Positions They Cannot Place
entry.summary: Knowing Which, Not How Much: Language Models Order Party Positions They Cannot Place arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines whether language models can place a political party's documented position on a numerical scale or can only rank parties relative to one another. Using party positions in Japan and South Korea, with coded data from the Comparative Manifesto Project as the answer key, the authors find models rank four parties well above a fixed-answer baseline. However, when asked to place one party on the same scale, they perform below that baseline, though supplying the coded values raises placement to near ceiling. ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate comparative ordering from absolute placement, testing Japanese and Korean party positions; models order far above baseline but place single parties below it.

entry.title: Parallel heavy-tailed convex optimization in ℓp norms with bias reduction
entry.summary: Bias-Reduced and Parallel Heavy-Tailed Stochastic Convex Optimization in ℓ_p Geometries arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies parallel stochastic convex optimization, where multiple stochastic gradient queries can be made per round, under heavy-tailed noise and ℓp geometries for 2 ≤ p < ∞. The authors introduce ODCp algorithms that combine stochastic bias-reduction with multilevel Monte Carlo methods, and a new p-GREG gradient estimator. These yield the parallel algorithms EpochDA and ℓp-AC-SA, with query depth bounds that improve on the sequential rate in a stated range of accuracy. The paper also gives dimension-dependent lower bounds for nonsmooth convex optimization over a subset of the unit ℓp ball. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose new ℓp optimal-distance algorithms and gradient estimator, improving parallel heavy-tailed query depth and giving dimension-dependent lower bounds.

entry.title: Quantum-classical separation in distribution transport via nonlocal games
entry.summary: Quantum-Classical Separation in Probability Distribution Transport via Nonlocal Games arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper asks whether local quantum dynamics can transport classical probability distributions in ways local classical dynamics cannot. The authors show that two classical distributions can be connected exactly and reversibly by a constant-depth local quantum circuit, while classical stochastic transport needs a substantially larger spatial range. The separation is demonstrated explicitly on a one-dimensional chain and generalized to graphs using a construction based on nonlocal games. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use nonlocal games to separate quantum from classical local transport, reporting constant-depth quantum circuits reversibly connecting classical distributions on a 1D chain.

entry.title: How much SAR vehicle recognition relies on the vehicle itself: background shortcuts, angle gaps and partial libraries
entry.summary: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines whether high accuracy on SAR vehicle recognition benchmarks comes from the vehicle itself. Using a ConvNeXt-Small network on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR, the authors show that accuracy stays well above chance even with the central vehicle region removed, and that background hurts accuracy under a scene-change split. They report that the gap between training and test depression angles mainly determines accuracy, and recommend reporting background-only and target-only controls. ★★★★ Notable: The authors systematically test background shortcuts, angle gaps, and partial libraries in SAR vehicle recognition on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR, reporting multi-seed results.

entry.title: SimAI: Psychology-Network-Based Simulation of Realistic User Behavior
entry.summary: SimAI: Mechanistic User Simulation through Psychological Network Models arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper introduces SimAI, a framework that simulates users by modeling how psychological factors interact to shape their responses, using a graph reconstruction objective to reward simulated conversations that reflect those relationships. The authors also build PSYCHE, a dataset of 18,576 profile-network pairs derived from 516 psychotherapy cases. Automatic evaluations and an interactive study with 30 mental-health professionals and trainees report that SimAI performs well on diversity, profile alignment, conversational authenticity, and clinical training utility. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce psychological network-driven user simulation with a graph reconstruction reward, report automatic evaluation and a 30-professional interactive study, and build an 18,576-pair dat

entry.title: Re-examining How Long AI-Agent Code Survives: Measurement Choices Shape the Conclusion
entry.summary: Revisiting the Survival of Agent-Attributed Code: How Measurement Choices Decide the Verdict arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper reanalyzes how long code added by AI coding agents survives after merge, using 854,139 lines from 2,802 merged pull requests across 215 repositories in the AIDev dataset. The authors vary nine measurement choices across five research questions and build a specification curve of 88 survival analyses. For code from human-supervised agents, mostly GitHub Copilot, the choices change only the effect size, while for the fully autonomous agent Devin, they determine the verdict. ★★★★ Notable: The authors vary nine measurement choices across 88 survival analyses on 854,139 lines from AIDev, showing that choices can flip the verdict and affect future study design.

entry.title: Every Camera Grows Up: Camera-Height Drift in Interactive Video World Models
entry.summary: Every Camera Grows Up: Camera-Height Regression in Interactive Video World Models arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines whether interactive video world models, which simulate views for embodied agents, keep the camera at its starting height during movement. It finds that six recent open-weight models gradually move the camera toward human eye level, a failure it calls camera-height regression. The authors introduce the EyeHeight benchmark and analyze causes, including human-centric video priors that contain few floor-level views. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors name and measure camera-height regression across six interactive video world models, tracing it to human-centric video priors with classifier-free guidance strengthening it.

entry.title: Separating Moral Circuits and Features in Language Models: Moral Content, Normative Judgment, or Cue Words?
entry.summary: Disambiguating Moral Circuits and Moral Features in Language Models: Moral content, normative judgment or cue words? Evidence from 14 models arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper examines which attention heads and sparse autoencoder features in language models shape their answers to moral prompts, and whether they respond to moral content, general normative judgment, or the word "morally." The authors built 227 minimal sentence pairs and tested 14 open-weight models with and without that word. They found that the heads affecting moral answers also serve other kinds of normative judgment, and that most SAE features respond mainly to the word "morally". ★★★★ Notable: The authors separate moral content, normative judgment and the cue word "morally" using 227 minimal pairs across 14 models, reporting shared evaluation circuits.

entry.title: Circulant Diffusion Layers: Cost Bounds and Rectangle Reuse
entry.summary: Circulant Diffusion Layers: Cost Bounds and Rectangle Reuse IACR ePrint · Nov 14, 2026This paper studies the addition cost of sparse invertible circulant matrices over F_2 and odd prime fields, measuring diffusion by branch numbers. It introduces lower bounds on general and rectangle-reuse circuit costs for general matrices, and uses cyclic structure to obtain cost classifications and explicit constructions. For weight-three circulants, the minimum costs in both models are 3n/2 at even orders over F_2 and ceil(3n/2) over odd prime fields. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give first lower bounds on general and rectangle costs and a complete classification with exact minima for weight-three circulants.

entry.title: Static lower bounds on thermal fast scrambling
entry.summary: Static Bounds on Thermal Fast Scrambling arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper proves logarithmic lower bounds on scrambling times at every fixed temperature for the SYK model and random k-local spin systems, without assuming real-time factorization. The method uses the operator-size distribution of the square root of the Gibbs state together with analyticity in complex time to bound the thermal correlator. The result is that scrambling time is at least (1-ε)[β/(2π)]log N with probability tending to one, matching the coefficient suggested by the chaos bound. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors use operator-size distributions of the Gibbs state's square root and complex-time analyticity to derive logarithmic scrambling-time lower bounds at any fixed temperature for SYK and random

entry.title: LABEL: Literature Asymmetry Between Efficacy and Limits in Drug Knowledge
entry.summary: LABEL: Literature Asymmetry between Efficacy and Limits in Drug Knowledge and Language Models arXiv · Nov 14, 2026The paper compares how often Wikipedia and PubMed texts mention a drug's indications versus its contraindications across 574 drugs. Contraindications are named far less often, with benefits mentioned about twice as frequently. As the Qwen2.5 models scale up, accuracy on indications improves while accuracy on contraindications stays near random. The authors suggest routing medication-safety questions to official regulatory labels and structured databases. ★★★★ Notable: The authors quantify an asymmetry between indications and contraindications in drug literature and link it to model safety failures, using 574 drugs and Qwen2.5 across scales.

entry.title: Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
entry.summary: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper uses a 105-qubit Willow superconducting processor to run and scale a surface code stability experiment that is sensitive to errors in time. It finds a temporally correlated error in which data qubits heat up to the third excited state, and models this effect with a parameter-free leakage model. The authors introduce a walking stability circuit that lowers the logical error floor to 3.20×10⁻⁸ at 60 cycles, and adaptive termination based on decoder confidence reduces spacetime logical error by 38%. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report a walking stability circuit addressing temporally correlated |3> heating errors, scaled to 7x7 patches on a 105-qubit superconducting processor, reaching a logical error floor.

entry.title: Optimal quantum sensing algorithms for spectroscopy over a known set of frequencies
entry.summary: Optimal Quantum Sensing Algorithms for Discrete-Frequency Spectroscopy arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper develops quantum sensing algorithms for discrete-frequency spectroscopy, where signals are drawn from a known set of N candidate frequencies. It designs optimal algorithms for Detection, Search, and Learning tasks, achieving a √N speedup over conventional frequency scanning. Simulations including experimental imperfections predict up to two orders of magnitude speedup for Detection, with applications discussed for molecular screening and weak-signal wireless communication. ★★★★ Notable: The authors design optimal quantum sensing algorithms for detection, search, and learning of discrete-frequency signals, reporting a √N speedup over frequency scanning, with simulations and a molecula

entry.title: Speed limit of gravity-induced entanglement and the cost of noise
entry.summary: The speed limit of gravitational entanglement and the cost of noise arXiv · Nov 17, 2026This paper studies how fast two small masses can become entangled through their mutual gravity, and what noise costs. Without noise, the maximum rate falls as the inverse cube of the separation and is reached with two positions per mass. Above a noise level, the rate is limited to fall at least as the inverse fourth power, and gravity's leading effect can be imitated by classical signals. Continuous error correction protects the masses from noise but reduces their mutual entanglement, with the best rate falling as the inverse seventh power. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive the exact maximum rate of gravitational entanglement without noise and quantify the noise cost, reporting optimal rates and thresholds in the abstract.

entry.title: Ideal correlations explain quantum theory's structure
entry.summary: Plenitude of ideal correlations explains quantum theory arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper shows that quantum theory's Hilbert-space formalism and Born rule follow from a single principle. In any theory where every observable admits an ideal measurement, every possible correlation is physically realizable. An ideal measurement gives the same outcome when repeated and does not disturb any compatible observable. ★★★★ Notable: The authors derive Hilbert-space formalism and the Born rule from a plenitude principle on ideal-measurement correlations, offering a new axiomatic route to quantum theory.

entry.title: Rethinking entropic uncertainty: how unrecorded measurements yield longer keys
entry.summary: Rethinking Entropic Uncertainty: How measuring without a trace leads to longer keys arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper proposes a new perspective for analyzing quantum key distribution security by treating Alice and Bob as one joint system and adding a third register that records virtual measurements. These virtual measurements leave no trace in the real protocol branch but condition counterfactual phase error measurements. The authors show this yields tight key rates directly from the entropic uncertainty relation for protocols using any number of mutually unbiased bases. They also indicate the approach can improve many existing security proofs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a virtual-measurement register as a third system, letting entropic uncertainty relations directly incorporate arbitrarily many MUBs with tight key rates.

entry.title: Information causality is violated at every finite NPA level, and by an unbounded amount
entry.summary: Information Causality Defeats Every Finite NPA Level arXiv · Nov 17, 2026The paper constructs, for each finite level of the NPA hierarchy, correlations that satisfy all of that level's constraints yet violate information causality. Quantum correlations obey the one-bit bound, while the optimal information gain at any fixed NPA level grows logarithmically with the number of measurement settings. The violation can grow without bound, and a single communicated bit suffices to expose this gap. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct correlations violating information causality at every finite NPA level, with the violation growing logarithmically in measurement settings.

entry.title: Ten-dimensional mutually unbiased bases: no complete set contains the Fourier pair or three product bases
entry.summary: No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in dimension ten contains the Fourier pair or three product bases arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) in ten-dimensional complex space, where it is unknown whether a complete set of eleven exists, and only three are known. The authors prove that any three mutually unbiased product bases of C²⊗C⁵ are strongly unextendible, so no set of four MUBs in dimension ten contains three product bases. They also show that the standard and Fourier bases cannot be contained in any set of four MUBs. The proofs rely on computer-assisted certificates, including Nullstellensatz and interval branch-and-bound methods. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report that triples of product MUBs in dimension ten are strongly unextendible and that the standard-Fourier pair lies in no four-MUB set, using computer-assisted certificates.

entry.title: Reversing dynamical backaction and cooling below the quantum backaction limit in Floquet-driven optomechanical resonators
entry.summary: Reversal of dynamical backaction and cooling below the quantum backaction limit in Floquet-driven multimode optomechanical resonators arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper studies how time-varying (Floquet) optical driving can strongly enhance dynamical backaction in multimode optomechanical resonators. The modulated drive couples a sideband-unresolved MHz mode to a sideband-resolved GHz mode through a shared cavity, so the auxiliary mode's occupancy replaces the quantum backaction limit of the target mode. In experiments, the MHz mode was cooled to 47 ± 13 phonons, about half its single-mode quantum backaction limit. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report cooling an MHz mode to 47 phonons below its single-mode QBA limit via Floquet coupling to an auxiliary GHz mode, plus a modulation-controlled cooling-amplification inversion.

entry.title: Closing the Loop on Memory: A Decoder for Quantum LDPC Codes
entry.summary: Closing the loop on memory: accurate, shallow and transferable decoding of quantum LDPC codes arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper introduces TEMPO-BP, a decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes that adjusts each variable's memory strength using local feedback from the decoding state. On the gross code at a 0.4% physical error rate, a single run achieves a 0.73% per-shot logical failure rate, versus 2.51% for BP+OSD+CS-10. Ensembles of 10 to 15 concurrent instances match or lower failure counts compared with Relay-BP-5 across ten tested operating points, using far lower per-instance iteration caps. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose TEMPO-BP, adapting per-variable memory strength via local feedback, and report lower logical failure rates than BP+OSD+CS-10 and Relay-BP-5 on the gross code.

entry.title: Rate-1/2 quantum LDPC codes for multi-tier superconducting hardware
entry.summary: Rate-1/2 Quantum LDPC Codes for Multi-tier Superconducting Hardware arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This paper introduces Armillary codes, a family of ultra-high-rate quantum LDPC codes whose structure is generated by native iSWAP routing under hardware constraints. The authors construct explicit codes with rates above 1/2, stabilizer weight 12, and distances from 12 to 16, laid out on 5 or 6 hardware tiers. Compared with Gross and Mitten codes at the same distances, they achieve encoding rates about 6 and 2.5 times higher. In circuit-level simulations, the [[8688,4348,16]] code reaches a logical error rate of 1.62×10⁻¹² per logical qubit per round at a physical error rate of 0.1%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes generated by native iSWAP routing on fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware, reporting circuit-level simulation results.

entry.title: Quantum-boosted radio-frequency optical imaging, passive and active
entry.summary: Quantum-Enhanced Passive and Active Radio-Frequency Photonic Imaging arXiv · Nov 16, 2026This study encodes radio-frequency signals onto a bright phase-squeezed optical carrier and reads them out with balanced homodyne detection, surpassing the standard quantum limit in both passive and active RF imaging. A unified model shows that phase squeezing reduces the readout noise variance by a single factor. In 5–20 MHz experiments, 3 dB of squeezing improved peak signal-to-noise ratio by about 6 dB, matching the model's predictions. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use phase-squeezed light to beat the standard quantum limit in RF photonic imaging, with a unified model validated experimentally in the 5–20 MHz band.

entry.title: A study showing one forward classical bit can replace error correction for amplitude-damping channels
entry.summary: A Forward Bit Makes Error Correction Dispensable for Antidegradable Amplitude-Damping Channels arXiv · Nov 16, 2026The paper studies how to preserve a qubit over an antidegradable amplitude-damping channel. The authors prove that one channel use with one forward classical bit matches or outperforms any forward-assisted or unassisted code with any number of uses. Variational circuit experiments show that as damping grows, the circuits shift from error correction to classical assistance, extending storage time relative to the best unassisted see-saw method. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove one channel use plus one forward bit matches any multi-use code, and report variational circuits beating unassisted three-use codes.
